The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(4x+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(4x+C) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(4(x+\frac{C}{4}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{C}{4}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(4(x+\frac{C}{4}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(4x).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/4c5147d95cc4d5df1d847f5fe9f580d9595d0f4d8c2c8209efa1f2a3cd9c5aea.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(4x)$ by $\frac{9\pi }{40}-\frac{\pi }{8}=\frac{\pi }{10}$ units to the right. Therefore:

$$
\frac{C}{4}=-\frac{\pi }{10}\,⟹\,C=-\frac{2\pi }{5}
$$
